question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Domain of a Hyperboloid
question.problem: Given the hyperboloid of one sheet $(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{9}=1$, find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
question.worked_solution:
From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ (x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-1 & =\frac{{z}^{2}}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{2} & =9((x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-1) \\ z & =\pm 3\sqrt{(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-1 & \ge 0 \\ (x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & \ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the exterior of the ellipse $(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}=1,$ which includes the boundary.

Therefore, the domain is

$$
{(x,y)\,:\,(x-2)^{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}\ge 1}.
$$

judgment.reasoning: All 16 mathematical answers agree with the answers stated in their own captured worked solutions. However, several solutions contain authored explanatory errors: q-74022 incorrectly calls the xz-plane ellipse an xy-plane ellipse; q-74910 says to substitute (-3,1,-1), although its calculation correctly uses (3,1,-1); q-74919 prints a minus sign instead of a plus sign in its initial substituted denominator; and q-74903 incorrectly claims that common factors cannot be canceled, although x cancels on the function's domain. These errors do not change the correct selections. Individually: q-164284 gives (y+6)^2=-15, so there are no real y-intercepts. q-35429 gives (x-2)^2=4, hence x=0,4. q-164303 has z=±4√(x²/4+y²/9+1), defined for every real pair. q-36465 requires (x-2)²+y²/4≥1. q-164376 sets z=0 to obtain x²-y²=1. q-74022 sets y=0 to obtain x²/3+z²/8=1. q-74913 has numerator 0 and denominator 2 at the limiting point. q-74910 gives √(3-1-1)=1. q-86868 simplifies to (x+1)/y and tends to 0. q-74919 simplifies to (x-y)/(x²+2) and tends to -1. q-129346 simplifies to √(x+y)+z and tends to 2. q-74960 simplifies to -(√x+y) and tends to -2. q-74903 has path limits 3/2 along y=x and 1/2 along y=-x, so its limit does not exist. q-129403 has path limits 1 along y=0 and 0 along y=x, so its limit does not exist. q-35927 gives x²/4=0, hence only the origin. q-164269 has vertex (0,3,-1) and its principal axis parallel to the x-axis, giving y=3 and z=-1.
